paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. You have a great high priest, and He is not a stranger to your life. Jesus was "tempted in every way that we are, yet was without sin" (Hebrews 4:15). He knows what it's like down here, and He has never once given in. That means He doesn't look at your weakness from far away. He gets it.

So what do you do with a high priest like that? You walk right up. The writer says, "Let us then approach the throne of grace with confidence, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help us in our time of need" (Hebrews 4:16). Confidence, baker! Not tiptoeing, not rehearsing your speech, not hoping nobody notices you came in. I spent years holding my breath every time light hit my corner of a dark drawer, and I'm telling you, this is a different kind of door.

And you can trust Him, because He didn't just grab the job. God called Him, as He called Aaron, and said, "You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek" (Hebrews 5:4-6). He prayed with loud cries and tears, and He learned obedience from what He suffered. He became "the source of eternal salvation to all who obey Him" (Hebrews 5:7-9). So hold firmly to what you profess (Hebrews 4:14), and when you need mercy, go get it.
